title: Void Ending in an Opposition to Saturn
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3, Book III chapter 1 and Book III chapter 8

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The opposition is the hardest figure the Moon can close on: the text grades it as extreme enmity, because the signs it joins stand opposed across all four natural qualities. It shares with the square the warnings that guard every election, and a Moon waning in light and faced by Saturn is the source's own example of a serious misfortune.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with an opposition to Saturn, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his weight and his cold. Saturn holds the power of retention, and when he is afflicted he is the gravest of the impediments: the science of law and profound knowledge, deep and occult properties, the building trades, and working the soil are his, with murky rivers, black mountains, deep wells, and desert places among his locations. Lead and iron are his metals, black his color, the bitter taste his own. Well disposed and direct, he gives purity, long life, standing, honor, riches, and durable inheritances; afflicted, he is the lord of poverty, misery, pain, and imprisonment.
